authoredNote: Every line_number below was TRANSCRIBED from a measured run through ASTEngine.getParser + RealHclAnalyzer.analyze (the same entry run-fixtures.ts uses) and then checked line by line against the fixture source. What makes them constraints rather than a snapshot is the forbid set: each entry is an independently-argued position the HCL grammar permits writing, so the fixture fails if the analyzer's line moves to any of them.
rationale: H1 (reviews/hcl/master-review.md). The grammar wraps arithmetic and comparison operands in `expression -> operation -> binary_operation`, whose children are the SAME variable_expr + get_attr sibling run an `expression` carries. The pre-fix path reader was gated on `node.type === "expression"`, so every reference inside an operation was dropped: `is_restored = var.db_snapshot_identifier != null` published nothing. Measured over 9,079 corpus files: 758 attributes with an operation-rooted expression, 1,670 missed references overall, recall 0.942414. The fix reads maximal CONSECUTIVE runs of path tokens from any node over ALL children, which is also what keeps `var.a + var.b` from welding into `var.a.var.b` — a defect the first version of the fix introduced and this fixture caught. HONESTY TIERS: every relationship carries metadata.evidenceClass on the M14 taxonomy — `structural` (containment and the public surface, read straight off the tree), `reference_qualified` (a fully-qualified Terraform address, never a bare-name guess), and `import_based` (a module's `source =`). HCL emits NO `usage_contextual` or `inferred` edge at all: every fact is read off the AST at confidence 1.0, so those tiers do not apply and their absence is the honest record rather than an omission. The module's `source` is published twice on purpose — as an ImportInfo the indexer persists as a dependency row, and as an `imports` edge the graph draws — which is the same pairing C uses for its include edges.
